The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.\n\n## File naming\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |\n\n## Services and state\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |\n| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |\n| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |\n| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |\n\n## Card state\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |\n| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |\n| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |\n\n\n## Events and React integration\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |\n| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |\n| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |\n| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |\n\r\n\n---STYLE---\r\n---\ninternalId: f2ec9e28-8064-4707-bce9-b62f24d57524\n---\n\n# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)\n\nHow to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.\n\n**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.\n\n**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.\n\n---\n\n## 1. How to consume the theme\n\n- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.\n- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.\n- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.\n- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.\n- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Role â†’ theme slot\n\nPick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:\n\n| Role | Theme slot |\n|---|---|\n| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |\n| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |\n| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |\n| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |\n| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |\n| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |\n| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |\n| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |\n| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |\n| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |\n| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |\n| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |\n| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |\n| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |\n| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |\n| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |\n| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |\n| Destructive action | `error.main` |\n| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |\n\nRules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Layout\n\n- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.\n- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.\n- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor pane `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` (the `minWidth: 0` is required so long content ellipsizes instead of blowing out the row).\n- **Panels (sidebar, editor card, dialogs):** column flex with stacked bands (header / [toolbar] / body / footer). The **body scrolls** (`overflow-y: auto; minHeight: 0`); header and footer are `flexShrink: 0` and never scroll away.\n- **Spacer pattern:** push trailing items with `<Box sx={{ flex: 1 }} />` rather than `margin-left: auto` sprinkled around, so rows stay predictable.\n- Use flex `gap` for spacing between siblings â€” don't hand-space with per-child margins.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Spacing, margin & size conventions\n\n- **4/8px grid, via `theme.spacing`.** page padding `2.5`; between columns `2`; inside columns / between related controls `1`; dialog body gap `2â€“2.25`; field labelâ†’control gap `~0.9` (7px).\n- **Margins:** prefer padding on containers + flex `gap` over element margins. Where a floating panel needs breathing room (e.g. editor card, toolbar inside a panel), use container padding (`p: 2 / 2.5`), not margins on the children.\n- **Fixed heights (px):** menu row 44, ribbon 52, status bar 32, section header 40, tab row 40, standard button / control 34, dense icon button 26â€“28, input 42.\n- **Fixed widths (px):** column 296, sidebar 280, search 260, standard dialog 480, wide/editor dialog 760.\n- **Radius family (px):** buttons/icon-buttons 8 (small 6â€“7), inputs 9, cards 10, columns/panels 12, dialogs/popups 14, chips/pills 99, color swatches 3. `borderRadius: 1` covers the 8 case; use explicit `'9px'` etc. for the others.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Borders & elevation\n\n- **Rest = border, not shadow.** Resting surfaces: `border: '1px solid'`, `borderColor: 'divider'`. Inputs use `custom.borderStrong`. **Shadow only when floating or lifted** (hover, drag, dialogs/popovers).\n- **Separation between bands:** a single 1px `divider` hairline. Don't stack a heavy rule *and* an outline â€” one line, let background contrast do the rest. Vertical separators inside toolbars: a 20px-tall `custom.borderStrong` rule.\n- **Elevation ladder (only where floating):** card hover `0 4px 12px rgba(16,24,40,0.12)`; dragging MUI `elevation 8` + `rotate(2deg)`; contained button `0 1px 2px rgba(16,24,40,0.15)`; dialog/popup `0 24px 60px rgba(16,24,40,0.28)`; scrim `rgba(16,24,40,0.45)` + `backdropFilter: blur(2px)`.\n- Set `MuiPaper.elevation: 0` and `MuiButton.disableElevation` globally in the theme; add the shadows above explicitly where the ladder calls for it.\n- **On dark backgrounds shadows read as nothing** â€” the theme already handles this by making hover raise `borderColor` (`custom.borderHover`) instead of relying on shadow.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Typography usage\n\nDrive everything from theme variants / `theme.typography`; avoid ad-hoc `fontSize`.\n\n- Titles/values/headings â†’ `text.primary`; body & labels â†’ `text.secondary`; meta â†’ `custom.text3`.\n- **Field labels:** a plain `Typography` (12px/600, `text.secondary`) placed **above** the control â€” **never** MUI floating/outlined `TextField` labels (they clash with the app's flat-label style).\n- **Section/column headers:** `Typography variant=\"overline\"` (uppercase, `letterSpacing ~0.7px`, `fontWeight 700`, `custom.colHead`).\n- **ID chips only** use monospace; everything else is the theme's default family.\n- `button.textTransform: 'none'` and `button.fontWeight: 600` are set in the theme â€” don't re-uppercase buttons.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Interaction states\n\nConsistent across all components; all colors from the theme:\n\n- **Ghost icon button** (`IconButton`): transparent â†’ hover `bgcolor: track` (or `background.paper` on a colored panel) + `color: primary.main`. Override MUI's default circular hover tint via `sx`.\n- **Outlined button:** `divider` border, `text.secondary` â†’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`.\n- **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`.\n- **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`.\n- **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`.\n- **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump).\n- **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text.\n- Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives)\n\n- **Buttons:** `Button variant=\"contained\"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant=\"outlined\"` = secondary; `variant=\"text\"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. Don't use `Link` or text `Button` where an action button belongs (that reproduces the old text-link look).\n- **Icons:** `@mui/icons-material` **Outlined** variants; `fontSize: 18` in 34px buttons, `16` in dense, `13â€“15` inline. Don't hand-draw SVG.\n- **ID chip:** monospace, accent text on `custom.primaryBg`/status tint, `radius 5, flexShrink: 0`.\n- **Count chip:** `background.paper` bg, 1px `divider`, radius 9â€“10, `custom.text3`.\n- **State dot:** 7â€“8px circle + `text-3` label; green (`success.main`) = active/saved/online.\n- **Search:** pill `TextField` (`borderRadius: 99`, `bgcolor: background.default`), search start-adornment, `âŒ˜K` keycap end-adornment.\n- **Select:** `size=\"small\"`, optional dot+name via `renderValue`; 42px / radius-9 frame. When a select has a tooltip, keep the tooltip available while the select is closed and explicitly hide it for the entire time the select menu is open so it cannot cover the first option.\n- **Menu / context menu:** all `Menu` / `MenuItem` dropdowns and right-click context menus are dense by default through the theme. Call sites must not set density; `Select` option lists inherit the same density.\n- **Segmented control** (view switch, formatting toolbar): `ToggleButtonGroup` on a `custom.track` background; selected segment `background.paper` + `0 1px 2px` shadow + `primary` text.\n- **Dialog / popup:** `Dialog`/`Popover` with `PaperProps` â†’ `background.paper`, 1px `divider`, radius 14, big shadow; scrim via `slotProps.backdrop` (blur + tint). Bands separated by hairlines; footer on a `background.default` bar with top hairline; actions right-aligned (outlined Cancel + contained CTA). `autoFocus` first field; submit on `Enter` (`âŒ˜/Ctrl+Enter` in a textarea); close on `Esc`/backdrop.\n- **Empty state:** dashed target â€” `1.5px dashed custom.borderStrong`, radius 10, centered icon + `custom.text4` label. No \"click to add\" placeholder blocks.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Definition of done for a new component\n\n1. Zero hardcoded hex / raw px colors â€” every value comes from `theme.palette` / `theme.shape` / `theme.spacing` / `theme.typography`.\n2. Correct roleâ†’slot mapping (Â§2); at most one `primary` CTA on the surface.\n3. Borders at rest, shadow only when floating (Â§5); bands split by a single hairline.\n4. Hover **and** focus states on every interactive element (Â§7); icon buttons have tooltip + `aria-label`.\n5. Body scrolls, header/footer pinned; `minWidth: 0` on flex children that hold long text.\n6. Toggle to dark mode and confirm nothing breaks â€” if it does, you hardcoded a color somewhere (Â§1).\n\nComponent-specific detail lives in `GUIDANCE.md` (theme definition + board/list/dialog), `CARD_POPUP_GUIDE.md`, `RUN_DIALOG_GUIDE.md`, and `SIDEBAR_ACTIONS_GUIDE.md`.\n\r\n\n---F194---\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_194\ninternalId: 4191dc0a-7628-45bf-ada1-b1366e9f05f9\ntitle: track token usage vs usage metrics\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__4191dc0a-7628-45bf-ada1-b1366e9f05f9.json\npolicy:\nafter: dffba4e6-6ec5-4a40-8ee7-e68d4891aff3\n---\n\nwe are currently already counting the tokens used by a project. we track this pretty granularly, but always related to the project: global total, per card, per action.\n\nwe also report 'account limits'. currently already working for codex, soon for claude likely too (see [F\\_193\\_report\\_claude\\_usage\\_quotas.md](design/feature_descriptions/F_193_report_claude_usage_quotas.md) )\n\nnow we want to measure and save both values (deltas) over time so we can track: how many tokens were used per hour, per day, per week and how much account limits shrank in the same period, so how much account usage there was.\n\nThis allows us to check how the relationship is between token usage and account usage at various hours and days.\n\ninfo should be saved in a csv file in the project folder\n\n## Current state\n\nNormalized token usage already flows through `AgentRunnerService` and is persisted cumulatively in each conversation activity file. Renderer aggregation in `app/src/services/agents/agent_usage.ts` derives totals per action, card, release, and project from those files. It has no observation timestamp per completed turn, so existing totals cannot produce reliable hourly, daily, or weekly deltas.\n\nCodex and Claude account usage are separate account-wide runtime snapshots in `CodexRuntimeService` and `ClaudeRuntimeService`. Each snapshot contains observed used percentages and reset times. Codex snapshots arrive from app-server rate-limit reads and updates; Claude snapshots arrive from `ClaudeUsagePoller`. Both remain in memory and are currently never written to project storage.\n\nProject token usage and account usage have different scopes. Token records cover this project's agent turns. Account records cover all use of that provider account, including other projects and external CLI sessions. Their time-based comparison is therefore correlation, not proof that this project caused an account-limit change.\n\n## implementation details\n\n* Add a desktop-owned usage-metrics service. Renderer components stay unchanged. Inject service into `AgentRunnerService`; do not derive history from renderer project totals.\n* Append records to `<projectFolder>/usage_metrics.csv`, resolving path inside repository root. Create file with one header when absent. Serialize writes per file so concurrent runs cannot interleave rows. Use RFC 4180 escaping and UTC ISO-8601 timestamps.\n* Use one CSV schema for two record types: `recorded_at`, `record_type`, `provider`, `limit_id`, `window_id`, `window_duration_minutes`, `resets_at`, `input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `used_percent`, `used_percent_delta`. Fields not applicable to record type remain empty, not zero.\n* Append one `token_usage` record after each successfully completed provider turn. Values are normalized turn usage, already a delta for that turn. Record streaming turns at `turnCompleted`; record one-shot turns after successful process completion. Do not subtract project totals, because reloads, moved cards, and archived releases can change those totals without new account usage.\n* Append one `account_usage` record per changed, available account window. Claude uses window ids `five_hour` and `weekly`, with limit id `default`. Codex uses each bucket's `limitId` plus `primary` or `secondary`; preserve `windowDurationMins`. Normalize reset timestamps to UTC milliseconds before CSV formatting.\n* Calculate `used_percent_delta` against previous persisted observation with same provider, limit id, and window id. First observation has empty delta because no baseline exists. Within same reset window, delta is current minus previous used percent. After reset time changes, delta equals current used percent because new window starts at zero. Preserve negative same-window corrections; do not clamp them.\n* Restore last valid account observation per key from existing CSV before first append so app restart does not discard delta baseline. Skip duplicate account observations whose percent and reset time are unchanged. Reject malformed rows for baseline purposes without rewriting existing file.\n* Carry project destination with Codex runtime events produced by a run. When Claude poll requests are coalesced, retain every requesting project destination and write resulting snapshot to each one. Concurrent projects can therefore contain same account observation; this matches account-wide scope.\n* Unavailable or malformed account snapshots create no metric row. Missing or invalid required token fields create no token row. Report read/append failures through existing desktop error reporting without failing or cancelling agent turn; later valid observations may retry.\n* Hour, day, and week totals are derived by grouping `recorded_at` in UTC and summing token fields or `used_percent_delta`. CSV stores raw deltas only; no rolling aggregate rows or UI are added.\n* Keep conversation usage persistence, current project/card/action totals, rate-limit bridges, and status indicators unchanged. Add desktop unit tests for schema/header creation, CSV escaping, serialized append, turn recording, provider window mapping, delta/reset rules, restart baseline recovery, duplicate suppression, malformed input, concurrent project destinations, and non-fatal I/O failure.\n\n## acceptance criteria\n\n* Successful Codex and Claude turns append exactly one `token_usage` record containing their normalized turn-token delta and UTC completion time.\n* Changed available Codex and Claude account windows append `account_usage` records with provider, stable bucket/window identity, reset time, used percent, and correctly calculated percent delta.\n* First account observation has empty delta; same-window observations use current minus previous percent; first observation after a known reset uses current percent from zero. Negative same-window corrections remain visible.\n* Restarting desktop restores each delta baseline from existing CSV. Repeated unchanged snapshots do not add rows.\n* Grouping records by UTC hour, day, or week yields token usage and observed account-usage change for same period without double-counting token values across account windows.\n* CSV is append-only, has one header, remains valid under concurrent agent runs, and exists at `<projectFolder>/usage_metrics.csv`.\n* Account activity outside project may affect account rows; documentation and field naming never describe account delta as usage caused by project.\n* Malformed/unavailable snapshots and CSV I/O failures do not crash, fail, or cancel agent runs. Existing conversation usage, status-bar limits, bridges, and renderer behavior remain unchanged.\n\r\n\n---F173---\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_173\ninternalId: bee2d3c7-81e1-451a-bc4d-d4ba59c849e9\ntitle: token count\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__bee2d3c7-81e1-451a-bc4d-d4ba59c849e9.json\npolicy:\nbranch: f_173_token_count\n---\nduring a release, the token count began to change up and down like crazy. clear indication that something is going wrong during the calculation of the token usage.\n\nWe should also perform a validation on the way that token count is calculated, we need to make certain that it is correct.\n\ntoken usage of released cards is no longer going to change. we can keep the summaries for these cards in more convenient places, like in a project wide json file for instance.\n\n## Current state\n\n`projectAgentTokenUsage` derives project and release totals from conversations currently attached to cards. Conversation loading is lazy, and release completion reparses moved cards. Totals can therefore rise or fall when activity files load or cards move, even when no new tokens were used.\n\nProvider normalization also overcounts some Codex usage. Codex cached input is part of provider `input_tokens`, and reasoning is part of provider `output_tokens`. Current streaming normalization keeps cached input inside `inputTokens`, while both Codex paths keep reasoning inside `outputTokens`; `totalTokens` then adds those overlapping buckets again.\n\nReleased activity files remain useful for opening one card's history, but released cards are read-only and their aggregate usage no longer needs repeated calculation.\n\nExisting activity files cannot always identify whether stored Codex input came from streaming or one-shot normalization. Their historical bucket split cannot be corrected reliably. Existing `totalTokens` must therefore remain a legacy baseline; corrected accounting starts with turns recorded after this change.\n\n## implementation details\n\n- Add `<projectFolder>/agent_token_usage.json` with `schemaVersion`, authoritative `projectUsage`, and immutable release entries keyed by release name. Each usage value contains preserved `legacyTotalTokens`, corrected `inputTokens`, `cachedInputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `reasoningTokens`, combined `totalTokens`, and optional `costUsd`. Do not store per-card summaries.\n- Define token buckets as disjoint. For Codex, subtract cached input from provider input and reasoning from provider output before storing their separate buckets. For Claude, keep cache creation and cache reads in `cachedInputTokens`; keep thinking in `outputTokens` while Claude does not report a separate reasoning count. Reject negative, non-finite, or inconsistent provider values. When provider total exists, verify normalized bucket sum matches it.\n- Make `projectUsage` the status-bar project's source of truth. Update it by the normalized delta only after a successful turn and conversation persistence. Serialize summary updates per project and update conversation activity plus summary in one commit so retries or concurrent turns cannot double-count or lose usage.\n- When summary file is absent in an existing project, read all card activity files once. Sum their stored `totalTokens` into `legacyTotalTokens`; do not reinterpret historical input, cache, output, or reasoning buckets. Set corrected buckets to zero, calculate project and existing-release summaries, and persist new file. For new projects, `legacyTotalTokens` starts at zero. A malformed existing summary is an error; do not silently rebuild or overwrite it.\n- Version conversation usage written after this change. When an existing conversation first continues, preserve its previous `totalTokens` as conversation-level legacy usage before accumulating corrected turn buckets. This keeps later release calculation able to separate legacy and corrected usage without adding per-card data to summary file.\n- During release, reject completion while a target card has a running action. Read target cards' activity files directly, calculate release usage, add one release entry, and commit summary update with card and activity-file moves. Existing release name remains an error. Moving cards does not change `projectUsage` because their usage was already counted.\n- Use stored release entries for release totals. Opening a released card may load its moved activity file for conversation detail, but that load must not change release or project totals.\n- Keep current and archived detail derived from their card activity. Do not add current, archived, action, or card summaries to `agent_token_usage.json`.\n- Add tests for Codex and Claude bucket semantics, provider-total validation, project-summary migration, malformed files, serialized/idempotent turn updates, concurrent turns, atomic release updates, active-run rejection, reloads, and opening released cards.\n\n## acceptance criteria\n\n- Project token total does not change when cards or activity files load, a released card opens, project reloads, or release files move.\n- Each successful persisted provider turn increases project total exactly once by normalized turn usage. Failed, cancelled, retried, or unpersisted turns add nothing.\n- Codex cached input and reasoning tokens appear in their own buckets without also remaining in input or output. Claude cache buckets are counted once, and Claude output remains correct when separate reasoning usage is unavailable.\n- For new usage, normalized bucket sum matches provider total when provider total exists. Summary `totalTokens` equals `legacyTotalTokens` plus corrected bucket sum. Invalid or overlapping new provider values produce a reported error instead of a wrong count.\n- Completing a release writes one immutable total for that release and leaves project total unchanged. Concurrent activity on target cards cannot race release calculation.\n- `agent_token_usage.json` contains only schema metadata, total project usage, and per-release usage. Card history and per-card usage remain retrievable from released activity files.\n- Existing projects without summary file receive one complete summary built from all card activity. Historical `totalTokens` is preserved as an explicitly named legacy baseline; only later turns claim corrected bucket accuracy.  }, [])\n\n    useEffect(() => {\n        const handleBeforeUnload = (event: BeforeUnloadEvent) => {\n            const staged = stageMarkdownEditors()\n            const { hasPendingPush, design\activity\card__8690b93e-98c4-486f-95b6-aacc10931a56.json:154:          "content": "---\nauthor: \nid: F_194\ninternalId: 4191dc0a-7628-45bf-ada1-b1366e9f05f9\ntitle: track token usage vs usage metrics\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__4191dc0a-7628-45bf-ada1-b1366e9f05f9.json\npolicy:\nafter: dffba4e6-6ec5-4a40-8ee7-e68d4891aff3\n---\n\nwe are currently already counting the tokens used by a project. we track this pretty granularly, but always related to the project: global total, per card, per action.\n\nwe also report 'account limits'. currently already working for codex, soon for claude likely too (see [F\\_193\\_report\\_claude\\_usage\\_quotas.md](design/feature_descriptions/F_193_report_claude_usage_quotas.md) )\n\nnow we want to measure and save both values (deltas) over time so we can track: how many tokens were used per hour, per day, per week and how much account limits shrank in the same period, so how much account usage there was.\n\nThis allows us to check how the relationship is between token usage and account usage at various hours and days.\n\ninfo should be saved in a csv file in the project folder\n\n## Current state\n\nNormalized token usage already flows through `AgentRunnerService` and is persisted cumulatively in each conversation activity file. Renderer aggregation in `app/src/services/agents/agent_usage.ts` derives totals per action, card, release, and project from those files. It has no observation timestamp per completed turn, so existing totals cannot produce reliable hourly, daily, or weekly deltas.\n\nCodex and Claude account usage are separate account-wide runtime snapshots in `CodexRuntimeService` and `ClaudeRuntimeService`. Each snapshot contains observed used percentages and reset times. Codex snapshots arrive from app-server rate-limit reads and updates; Claude snapshots arrive from `ClaudeUsagePoller`. Both remain in memory and are currently never written to project storage.\n\nProject token usage and account usage have different scopes. Token records cover this project's agent turns. Account records cover all use of that provider account, including other projects and external CLI sessions. Their time-based comparison is therefore correlation, not proof that this project caused an account-limit change.\n\n## implementation details\n\n* Add a desktop-owned usage-metrics service. Renderer components stay unchanged. Inject service into `AgentRunnerService`; do not derive history from renderer project totals.\n* Append records to `<projectFolder>/usage_metrics.csv`, resolving path inside repository root. Create file with one header when absent. Serialize writes per file so concurrent runs cannot interleave rows. Use RFC 4180 escaping and UTC ISO-8601 timestamps.\n* Use one CSV schema for two record types: `recorded_at`, `record_type`, `provider`, `limit_id`, `window_id`, `window_duration_minutes`, `resets_at`, `input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `used_percent`, `used_percent_delta`. Fields not applicable to record type remain empty, not zero.\n* Append one `token_usage` record after each successfully completed provider turn. Values are normalized turn usage, already a delta for that turn. Record streaming turns at `turnCompleted`; record one-shot turns after successful process completion. Do not subtract project totals, because reloads, moved cards, and archived releases can change those totals without new account usage.\n* Append one `account_usage` record per changed, available account window. Claude uses window ids `five_hour` and `weekly`, with limit id `default`. Codex uses each bucket's `limitId` plus `primary` or `secondary`; preserve `windowDurationMins`. Normalize reset timestamps to UTC milliseconds before CSV formatting.\n* Calculate `used_percent_delta` against previous persisted observation with same provider, limit id, and window id. First observation has empty delta because no baseline exists. Within same reset window, delta is current minus previous used percent. After reset time changes, delta equals current used percent because new window starts at zero. Preserve negative same-window corrections; do not clamp them.\n* Restore last valid account observation per key from existing CSV before first append so app restart does not discard delta baseline. Skip duplicate account observations whose percent and reset time are unchanged. Reject malformed rows for baseline purposes without rewriting existing file.\n* Carry project destination with Codex runtime events produced by a run. When Claude poll requests are coalesced, retain every requesting project destination and write resulting snapshot to each one. Concurrent projects can therefore contain same account observation; this matches account-wide scope.\n* Unavailable or malformed account snapshots create no metric row. Missing or invalid required token fields create no token row. Report read/append failures through existing desktop error reporting without failing or cancelling agent turn; later valid observations may retry.\n* Hour, day, and week totals are derived by grouping `recorded_at` in UTC and summing token fields or `used_percent_delta`. CSV stores raw deltas only; no rolling aggregate rows or UI are added.\n* Keep conversation usage persistence, current project/card/action totals, rate-limit bridges, and status indicators unchanged. Add desktop unit tests for schema/header creation, CSV escaping, serialized append, turn recording, provider window mapping, delta/reset rules, restart baseline recovery, duplicate suppression, malformed input, concurrent project destinations, and non-fatal I/O failure.\n\n## acceptance criteria\n\n* Successful Codex and Claude turns append exactly one `token_usage` record containing their normalized turn-token delta and UTC completion time.\n* Changed available Codex and Claude account windows append `account_usage` records with provider, stable bucket/window identity, reset time, used percent, and correctly calculated percent delta.\n* First account observation has empty delta; same-window observations use current minus previous percent; first observation after a known reset uses current percent from zero. Negative same-window corrections remain visible.\n* Restarting desktop restores each delta baseline from existing CSV. Repeated unchanged snapshots do not add rows.\n* Grouping records by UTC hour, day, or week yields token usage and observed account-usage change for same period without double-counting token values across account windows.\n* CSV is append-only, has one header, remains valid under concurrent agent runs, and exists at `<projectFolder>/usage_metrics.csv`.\n* Account activity outside project may affect account rows; documentation and field naming never describe account delta as usage caused by project.\n* Malformed/unavailable snapshots and CSV I/O failures do not crash, fail, or cancel agent runs. Existing conversation usage, status-bar limits, bridges, and renderer behavior remain unchanged.\n\r\n\n---CARD VIEW---\r\nimport { Box } from '@mui/material'\nimport { DndContext, DragOverlay, PointerSensor, closestCorners, useSensor, useSensors } from '@dnd-kit/core'\nimport type { DragEndEvent, DragOverEvent, DragStartEvent } from '@dnd-kit/core'\nimport { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'\nimport { buildCardColumns } from '../../data/card_ordering'\nimport type { CardTypeConfig, StateConfig } from '../../data/data_types'\nimport { dataService } from '../../services/data/data_service'\nimport { dialogService } from '../../services/dialog_service'\nimport { openFilesService } from '../../services/open_files_service'\nimport { workspaceViewService } from '../../services/project/workspace_view_service'\nimport { telemetryService } from '../../services/telemetry/telemetry_service'\nimport { AffectsEditorDialog } from './affects_editor_dialog'\nimport { CardBodyPopover } from './card_body_popover'\nimport { cardPopupService } from '../../services/card_popup_service'\nimport { CardColumn } from './card_column'\nimport { CardDragOverlay } from './card_drag_overlay'\nimport { cardDragDropService } from './card_drag_drop_service'\nimport { resolveCardDragEvent } from './card_drag'\nimport { useCardViewColumns } from './use_card_view_columns'\n\nconst DRAG_ACTIVATION_DISTANCE = 2\ninterface CardViewProps {\n    cardTypes: CardTypeConfig[]\n    states: StateConfig[]\n    statusColors: Map<string, string>\n}\n\nasync function runCardEdit(action: () => unknown, fallbackMessage: string) {\n    try {\n        await action()\n    } catch (error) {\n        dialogService.error(error, { fallbackMessage })\n    }\n}\n\nfunction currentCardColumns(states: StateConfig[]) {\n    const cards = dataService.getState().snapshot?.activeCards ?? []\n\n    return buildCardColumns(cards, states)\n}\n\n/** Card view: status columns of draggable cards with card-anchored body popup access. */\nexport function CardView(props: CardViewProps) {\n    const {\n        cardTypes,\n        states,\n        statusColors,\n    } = props\n    const columns = useCardViewColumns(states)\n    const [openAffectsPath, setOpenAffectsPath] = useState<string | null>(null)\n    const rootElementRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)\n    const dragColumnsRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof currentCardColumns> | null>(null)\n    const lastOverIdRef = useRef<string | null>(null)\n    const missingRootReportedRef = useRef(false)\n    const wasVisibleRef = useRef<boolean | null>(null)\n    const sensors = useSensors(useSensor(PointerSensor, { activationConstraint: { distance: DRAG_ACTIVATION_DISTANCE } }))\n\n    const handleOpenAffects = (path: string) => {\n        setOpenAffectsPath(path)\n    }\n\n    const handleCloseAffects = () => {\n        setOpenAffectsPath(null)\n    }\n\n    const clearActiveCard = useCallback(() => {\n        dragColumnsRef.current = null\n        lastOverIdRef.current = null\n        cardDragDropService.endDrag()\n    }, [])\n\n    useEffect(() => {\n        const updateVisibility = () => {\n            const rootElement = rootElementRef.current\n            if (!rootElement) {\n                if (!missingRootReportedRef.current) {\n                    missingRootReportedRef.current = true\n                    dialogService.error(new Error('Missing card view root element'), {fallbackMessage: 'Card view could not be displayed'})\n                }\n                return\n            }\n\n            const isVisible = workspaceViewService.getSnapshot().viewMode === 'cards'\n            rootElement.style.display = isVisible ? 'flex' : 'none'\n            if (wasVisibleRef.current === isVisible) return\n\n            wasVisibleRef.current = isVisible\n            if (isVisible) return\n\n            queueMicrotask(() => {\n                cardPopupService.closeCardDetails()\n                setOpenAffectsPath((currentPath) => currentPath === null ? currentPath : null)\n                clearActiveCard()\n            })\n        }\n\n        updateVisibility()\n        workspaceViewService.addEventListener('changed', updateVisibility)\n\n        return () => workspaceViewService.removeEventListener('changed', updateVisibility)\n    }, [clearActiveCard])\n\n    useEffect(() => () => cardPopupService.closeCardDetails(), [])\n\n    const handleDragStart = useCallback((event: DragStartEvent) => {\n        dragColumnsRef.current = currentCardColumns(states)\n        lastOverIdRef.current = null\n        cardDragDropService.startDrag(\n            String(event.active.id),\n            event.active.rect.current.initial?.height ?? null,\n            event.active.rect.current.initial?.width ?? null,\n        )\n    }, [states])\n\n    const handleDragOver = useCallback((event: DragOverEvent) => {\n        const { active, over } = event\n        const overId = over ? String(over.id) : null\n        if (lastOverIdRef.current === overId) return\n\n        lastOverIdRef.current = overId\n        if (!over) {\n            cardDragDropService.setDropPreview(null)\n            return\n        }\n\n        const dragColumns = dragColumnsRef.current\n        if (!dragColumns) throw new Error('Cannot update a card drop target before dragging starts')\n\n        const drop = resolveCardDragEvent(dragColumns, event)\n        const sourceColumn = dragColumns.find((column) => column.cards.some((card) => card.path === String(active.id)))\n        const dropPreview = drop && sourceColumn?.status !== drop.targetStatus ? drop : null\n        cardDragDropService.setDropPreview(dropPreview)\n    }, [])\n\n    const handleDragEnd = useCallback((event: DragEndEvent) => {\n        const { active, over } = event\n        const drop = over ? resolveCardDragEvent(currentCardColumns(states), event) : null\n        const path = String(active.id)\n        if (!drop) {\n            clearActiveCard()\n            return\n        }\n\n        clearActiveCard()\n        void runCardEdit(() => dataService.cards.moveCard(path, drop.targetStatus, drop.targetIndex), `Card move failed: ${path}`)\n    }, [clearActiveCard, states])\n\n    const handleOpenInFileMode = (path: string) => {\n        cardPopupService.closeCardDetails()\n        workspaceViewService.selectPath(path)\n        void runCardEdit(() => openFilesService.openPath(path), `File open failed: ${path}`)\n        workspaceViewService.setViewMode('text')\n        telemetryService.trackEvent('navigation')\n    }\n\n    const handleDeleteCard = async (path: string) => {\n        try {\n            await dataService.cards.deleteCard(path)\n            workspaceViewService.clearSelectedPath(path)\n            cardPopupService.closeCardDetailsPath(path)\n            if (openAffectsPath === path) handleCloseAffects()\n        } catch (error) {\n            dialogService.error(error, { fallbackMessage: `Card delete failed: ${path}` })\n            throw error\n        }\n    }\n\n    const handleTitleChange = (path: string, title: string) => {\n        dataService.cards.updateCardTitle(path, title).catch((error: unknown) => {\n            dialogService.error(error, { fallbackMessage: `Title update failed: ${path}` })\n        })\n    }\n\n    const handleTogglePolicy = (path: string, policyKey: string) => {\n        void runCardEdit(() => dataService.cards.toggleCardPolicy(path, policyKey), `Policy toggle failed: ${path}`)\n    }\n\n    const handleAffectsChange = (path: string, affects: string[]) => {\n        void runCardEdit(() => dataService.cards.updateCardAffects(path, affects), `Affects update failed: ${path}`)\n    }\n\n    return (\n        <Box\n            ref={rootElementRef}\n            sx={{ bgcolor: 'background.default', display: 'flex', flex: 1, minHeight: 0, overflow: 'hidden', position: 'relative' }}\n onDragOver={handleDragOver}\n                onDragStart={handleDragStart}\n                sensors={sensors}\n            >\n                <Box\n                    aria-label=\"Card columns\"\n                    sx={{\n                        alignItems: 'flex-start',\n                        display: 'flex',\n                        flex: 1,\n                        flexDirection: 'row',\n cardTypes={cardTypes}\n                            column={column}\n                            isMobile={false}\n                            onDeleteCard={handleDeleteCard}\n                            onOpenInFileMode={handleOpenInFileMode}\n                            onTitleChange={handleTitleChange}\n                            onTogglePolicy={handleTogglePolicy}\n                        />\n  visible\n                />\n                <AffectsEditorDialog\n                    cardPath={openAffectsPath}\n                    onClose={handleCloseAffects}\n design\activity\card__bee2d3c7-81e1-451a-bc4d-d4ba59c849e9.json:668:          "content": "---\nauthor: \nid: F_194\ninternalId: 4191dc0a-7628-45bf-ada1-b1366e9f05f9\ntitle: track token usage vs usage metrics\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__4191dc0a-7628-45bf-ada1-b1366e9f05f9.json\npolicy:\nafter: dffba4e6-6ec5-4a40-8ee7-e68d4891aff3\n---\n\nwe are currently already counting the tokens used by a project. we track this pretty granularly, but always related to the project: global total, per card, per action.\n\nwe also report 'account limits'. currently already working for codex, soon for claude likely too (see [F\\_193\\_report\\_claude\\_usage\\_quotas.md](design/feature_descriptions/F_193_report_claude_usage_quotas.md) )\n\nnow we want to measure and save both values (deltas) over time so we can track: how many tokens were used per hour, per day, per week and how much account limits shrank in the same period, so how much account usage there was.\n\nThis allows us to check how the relationship is between token usage and account usage at various hours and days.\n\ninfo should be saved in a csv file in the project folder\n\n## Current state\n\nNormalized token usage already flows through `AgentRunnerService` and is persisted cumulatively in each conversation activity file. Renderer aggregation in `app/src/services/agents/agent_usage.ts` derives totals per action, card, release, and project from those files. It has no observation timestamp per completed turn, so existing totals cannot produce reliable hourly, daily, or weekly deltas.\n\nCodex and Claude account usage are separate account-wide runtime snapshots in `CodexRuntimeService` and `ClaudeRuntimeService`. Each snapshot contains observed used percentages and reset times. Codex snapshots arrive from app-server rate-limit reads and updates; Claude snapshots arrive from `ClaudeUsagePoller`. Both remain in memory and are currently never written to project storage.\n\nProject token usage and account usage have different scopes. Token records cover this project's agent turns. Account records cover all use of that provider account, including other projects and external CLI sessions. Their time-based comparison is therefore correlation, not proof that this project caused an account-limit change.\n\n## implementation details\n\n* Add a desktop-owned usage-metrics service. Renderer components stay unchanged. Inject service into `AgentRunnerService`; do not derive history from renderer project totals.\n* Append records to `<projectFolder>/usage_metrics.csv`, resolving path inside repository root. Create file with one header when absent. Serialize writes per file so concurrent runs cannot interleave rows. Use RFC 4180 escaping and UTC ISO-8601 timestamps.\n* Use one CSV schema for two record types: `recorded_at`, `record_type`, `provider`, `limit_id`, `window_id`, `window_duration_minutes`, `resets_at`, `input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `used_percent`, `used_percent_delta`. Fields not applicable to record type remain empty, not zero.\n* Append one `token_usage` record after each successfully completed provider turn. Values are normalized turn usage, already a delta for that turn. Record streaming turns at `turnCompleted`; record one-shot turns after successful process completion. Do not subtract project totals, because reloads, moved cards, and archived releases can change those totals without new account usage.\n* Append one `account_usage` record per changed, available account window. Claude uses window ids `five_hour` and `weekly`, with limit id `default`. Codex uses each bucket's `limitId` plus `primary` or `secondary`; preserve `windowDurationMins`. Normalize reset timestamps to UTC milliseconds before CSV formatting.\n* Calculate `used_percent_delta` against previous persisted observation with same provider, limit id, and window id. First observation has empty delta because no baseline exists. Within same reset window, delta is current minus previous used percent. After reset time changes, delta equals current used percent because new window starts at zero. Preserve negative same-window corrections; do not clamp them.\n* Restore last valid account observation per key from existing CSV before first append so app restart does not discard delta baseline. Skip duplicate account observations whose percent and reset time are unchanged. Reject malformed rows for baseline purposes without rewriting existing file.\n* Carry project destination with Codex runtime events produced by a run. When Claude poll requests are coalesced, retain every requesting project destination and write resulting snapshot to each one. Concurrent projects can therefore contain same account observation; this matches account-wide scope.\n* Unavailable or malformed account snapshots create no metric row. Missing or invalid required token fields create no token row. Report read/append failures through existing desktop error reporting without failing or cancelling agent turn; later valid observations may retry.\n* Hour, day, and week totals are derived by grouping `recorded_at` in UTC and summing token fields or `used_percent_delta`. CSV stores raw deltas only; no rolling aggregate rows or UI are added.\n* Keep conversation usage persistence, current project/card/action totals, rate-limit bridges, and status indicators unchanged. Add desktop unit tests for schema/header creation, CSV escaping, serialized append, turn recording, provider window mapping, delta/reset rules, restart baseline recovery, duplicate suppression, malformed input, concurrent project destinations, and non-fatal I/O failure.\n\n## acceptance criteria\n\n* Successful Codex and Claude turns append exactly one `token_usage` record containing their normalized turn-token delta and UTC completion time.\n* Changed available Codex and Claude account windows append `account_usage` records with provider, stable bucket/window identity, reset time, used percent, and correctly calculated percent delta.\n* First account observation has empty delta; same-window observations use current minus previous percent; first observation after a known reset uses current percent from zero. Negative same-window corrections remain visible.\n* Restarting desktop restores each delta baseline from existing CSV. Repeated unchanged snapshots do not add rows.\n* Grouping records by UTC hour, day, or week yields token usage and observed account-usage change for same period without double-counting token values across account windows.\n* CSV is append-only, has one header, remains valid under concurrent agent runs, and exists at `<projectFolder>/usage_metrics.csv`.\n* Account activity outside project may affect account rows; documentation and field naming never describe account delta as usage caused by project.\n* Malformed/unavailable snapshots and CSV I/O failures do not crash, fail, or cancel agent runs. Existing conversation usage, status-bar limits, bridges, and renderer behavior remain unchanged.\n\r\n",

import { cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react'
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { DEFAULT_PROJECT_CONFIG, type ProjectConfig, type StorageService } from '../../data/data_types'
import { projectStatsService } from '../../services/stats/project_stats_service'
import { AppThemeProvider } from '../../theme/theme_provider'
import { DialogDisplay } from '../dialog_display'
import { StatsContent } from './stats_content'

const metricsHeader = [
    'recorded_at', 'record_type', 'provider', 'limit_id', 'window_id', 'window_duration_minutes',
    'resets_at', 'input_tokens', 'cached_input_tokens', 'output_tokens', 'reasoning_tokens',
    'total_tokens', 'used_percent', 'used_percent_delta',
].join(',')
const config: ProjectConfig = {
    ...DEFAULT_PROJECT_CONFIG,
    actionsFolder: 'design/actions',
    archivedFolder: 'design/archived',
    projectFolder: 'design',
    releasesFolder: 'design/history',
    workingFolder: 'design/active',
}

function storage(content: string): StorageService {
    return {
        checkoutBranch: vi.fn(), commit: vi.fn(), createProject: vi.fn(), deleteFile: vi.fn(), deleteFolder: vi.fn(),
        listBranches: vi.fn(), listRepositories: vi.fn(), listRepositoryFiles: vi.fn(async () => ['design/usage_metrics.csv']),
        listTopLevelFolders: vi.fn(), loadActionFiles: vi.fn(), loadProject: vi.fn(), loadProjectConfig: vi.fn(),
        loadProjectRoot: vi.fn(), loadTextFile: vi.fn(async () => ({ content, path: 'design/usage_metrics.csv' })),
        moveFiles: vi.fn(), push: vi.fn(), saveProjectConfig: vi.fn(),
    }
}

function renderContent() {
    return render(<AppThemeProvider><DialogDisplay /><StatsContent /></AppThemeProvider>)
}

describe('StatsContent', () => {
    afterEach(() => cleanup())

    it('shows controls, local bucket label, UTC accessibility text, and current chart values', async () => {
        const metrics = `${metricsHeader}\r\n2026-08-12T10:00:00.000Z,token_usage,codex,,,,,3,2,4,1,10,,\r\n`
        projectStatsService.setControls({
            activityMetric: 'tokens', dataset: 'activityOverTime', endUtc: null, granularity: 'day', startUtc: null,
            totalsGrouping: 'card', totalsMetric: 'duration',
        })
        projectStatsService.bindProject({ config, project: { branch: 'main', id: 'project' }, storage: storage(metrics) })
        await projectStatsService.open([])
        renderContent()

        expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Project stats' })).toBeInTheDocument()
        expect(screen.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Dataset' })).toHaveTextContent('Activity over time')
        expect(screen.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveAccessibleName(/10 tokens.*UTC bucket boundary 2026-08-12T00:00:00.000Z/u)

        fireEvent.mouseDown(screen.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Granularity' }))
        fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('option', { name: 'Month' }))
        expect(projectStatsService.getSnapshot().controls.granularity).toBe('month')
    })

    it('renders and reports malformed-source errors without partial chart data', async () => {
        projectStatsService.bindProject({ config, project: { branch: 'main', id: 'project' }, storage: storage('broken') })
        await projectStatsService.open([])
        renderContent()

        expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Stats unavailable' })).toBeInTheDocument()
        await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByLabelText('Error message')).toHaveTextContent('Invalid usage metrics CSV header'))
        expect(screen.queryByRole('listitem')).toBeNull()
    })

    it('shows valid token data with a warning when malformed account usage is skipped', async () => {
        const malformedAccountRow = '2026-08-12T09:00:00.000Z,account_usage,codex,weekly,window,0,broken,,,,,,50,'
        const tokenRow = '2026-08-12T10:00:00.000Z,token_usage,codex,,,,,3,2,4,1,10,,'
        projectStatsService.setControls({ activityMetric: 'tokens', dataset: 'activityOverTime' })
        projectStatsService.bindProject({
            config,
            project: { branch: 'main', id: 'warning-project' },
            storage: storage(`${metricsHeader}\r\n${malformedAccountRow}\r\n${tokenRow}\r\n`),
        })
        await projectStatsService.open([])
        renderContent()

        expect(screen.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveAccessibleName(/10 tokens/u)
        expect(screen.getAllByText('Malformed account_usage row 2 was skipped.').length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
        await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByLabelText('Error message')).toHaveTextContent('Malformed account_usage row 2 was skipped.'))
    })
})
